clue.text: Dandy's top clothing company ranking third

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap round it, so the top here is worn around the company and the rank

parts.note: a top or summit is a peak
a C grade ranks third after A and B

explanation.surface: A dapper man's best outfit comes from a fashion house rated only third best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dandy's' reads as a possessive; the 's is just 'is'. 'Clothing' looks like garments but says one piece wraps the others; 'ranking third' is a C grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy, vain man fond of fine clothes is called after the strutting bird with the spectacular tail.

clue.text: See 19
Good-looker from Ulster during Troubles?

indicators.note: during puts the region inside the period of fuss

parts.note: ados are fusses or troubles
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster

explanation.surface: A handsome man from Northern Ireland in the time of the Troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Troubles' was the Northern Ireland conflict, but here troubles are just fusses.
explanation.definitionFit: The beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite gives his name to any very handsome man.

clue.text: Accomplished women's crew on the hefty side?

parts.note: something over is finished or accomplished
W is the abbreviation for women
an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A finished women's rowing crew that is a bit on the heavy side.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying too many pounds is being heavier than ideal, a phrase rendering of hefty.

clue.text: County's opener grabbing a couple of runs

indicators.note: grabbing means holding, so the opener holds the runs inside

parts.note: a key opens a lock
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs, so two of them

explanation.surface: A county cricket opener piles up a couple of runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' suggests an opening batsman; it is a key. KERRY is a county in the south-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, in Munster.

clue.text: Keep an eye on pillock appearing in dock

indicators.note: the fool shows up inside the berth, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to moor a boat is to dock it
a pillock is a British slang word for a fool, as is nit

explanation.surface: Watch out for an idiot turning up in the dock at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a courtroom, but here it is a verb for tying up a boat. PILLOCK is mild British slang for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over or observe something closely is a synonym-level match for this verb.

clue.text: Generator from England held up by hospital officer

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so the nurse word wraps round the country

parts.note: a matron was the senior nurse in a British hospital

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A power generator from England kept back by a hospital official.
explanation.definitionFit: This vacuum tube generates microwaves, in radar and microwave ovens.

clue.text: Duck seen on European river

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing

explanation.surface: A duck spotted on a river in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck is not a bird but a cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The great African waterway, the longest on the continent.

clue.text: Oppressor beheaded innocent queen after communist uprising

indicators.note: after says the trimmed word and queen come behind the communist
in a down clue an uprising reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a Trot is a Trotskyist, a type of communist

indicators.note: the first letter is cut from the word

parts.note: pure means innocent
R stands for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A tyrant executed a blameless queen after a communist revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' takes P off PURE to give URE; 'uprising' turns TROT to TORT.
explanation.definitionFit: One who inflicts cruel pain is an oppressor in an extreme sense.

clue.text: Cavalier fighter allegedly the greatest in stirring story

indicators.note: the boxer sits inside the shuffled letters
stirring means mixing up, so the letters of story are reordered

parts.note: boxer Muhammad Ali famously claimed I am the greatest

explanation.surface: A Civil War soldier featured in an exciting tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' looks like 'exciting' but it mixes STORY into ROYST. Cavaliers were the King's supporters in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavaliers fought for Charles I, so a supporter of the crown.

clue.text: Cure what many addicts do

definitions.meaning: to preserve fish or meat over a fire is to cure it this way

explanation.surface: A treatment that would get many addicts off their habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Curing kippers or bacon over burning wood is one sense; puffing tobacco is the other.

clue.text: Criminal goes missing from rogues' gallery surprisingly often

indicators.note: criminal, used of the word goes, says its letters are bent into a new order
the letters of goes are taken away from the rogues' gallery letters
surprisingly says the letters left over are jumbled into the answer

explanation.surface: A wanted man vanishes from the police photo collection with surprising frequency.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: take the letters of GOES (shuffled, 'Criminal') away from ROGUESGALLERY and rearrange the rest ('surprisingly'). A rogues' gallery is a police collection of mugshots.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at frequent, steady intervals happens often; the adverbs are near-synonyms.

clue.text: Phoney war mainly involving Eastern transport workers

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the shuffled letters close around the extra letter
phoney means fake, so the letters of war and mainly are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Phoney War of 1939-40 mostly drew in eastern transport workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Phoney War was the quiet early months of the Second World War; 'Phoney' here is only the anagram signal, and 'involving' wraps the shuffle round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Those employed on the trains and tracks are a classic category of transport staff.

clue.text: Arena where speculator meets syndicate

parts.note: on the stock market a bull is a speculator betting on rising prices
a ring is a group or cartel acting together

explanation.surface: An arena where a market speculator joins a business syndicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' and 'meets' simply join the pieces. A bull on the Stock Exchange is someone buying in expectation of a rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular arena for bullfighting is called by this name, as is a famous Birmingham shopping area.

clue.text: Who's today's setter? I've no answer to that

definitions.meaning: the setter is Nutmeg, so the solver has Nutmeg, written as having me
a casual phrase admitting one is stumped

explanation.surface: A puzzled solver asks who set the puzzle and admits being stumped.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter, Nutmeg, speaks of themself: the solver has 'me'. It is the same phrase as the shrug of the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a shrug admitting defeat, and literally the solver holds the setter.

clue.text: Ditching his date, musical man Spice Girl dancing

parts.note: Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the pop group the Spice Girls

indicators.note: ditching means dropping, so a letter is thrown out of the composer's name

parts.note: Richard Rodgers wrote stage musicals with Hammerstein
D is the standard abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A composer drops his date for a dancing Spice Girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Nutmeg said a word ('joins') went missing from the printed clue, which explains why the order of the two pieces is not signalled. The definition points loosely at the famous dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: The film star famous for dancing with Fred Astaire is evoked by the dancing at the end of the clue.

clue.text: Explosive sound of impact in German sub?

indicators.note: the bang goes inside the word for below

parts.note: sub as a prefix means beneath
pow imitates a blow landing

explanation.surface: An explosion's bang hits a German U-boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German sub' suggests a U-boat; 'sub' is UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: This black blasting mixture of saltpetre, charcoal and sulphur is the classic explosive.

clue.text: Journalist keeps married couple covered

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the editor wraps round the rest

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
a brace is a pair

explanation.surface: A reporter keeps a newly wed couple's story under wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken in or included by a scheme is said to be covered by it.

clue.text: Informant tipped off Busted's lead singer

indicators.note: busted means broken, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the tip, or first letter, is taken off the word

explanation.surface: A grass tipped off police about the singer of pop band Busted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped off' loses the I of INFORMANT; 'Busted' (a British pop band, here broken) scrambles the rest. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer who fronts a band is its lead vocalist.

clue.text: Long-haul traders in pity employing hard worker reversing vehicle

indicators.note: to employ is to take on, so the pity word holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: mercy is compassion or pity
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

indicators.note: the van backs up, so its letters are read the other way round

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A sad scene of a labourer backing a van, seen by long-distance hauliers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's commercial shipping fleet carries goods on long sea voyages, so it is a body of traders.

clue.text: European office workers sample food from bakery

parts.note: a Dane is from Denmark, a European country
PAs are personal assistants
to try something is to sample it

explanation.surface: Office workers from Europe try out some cakes from the bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet flaky pastry with fruit or icing sold in bakeries.

clue.text: Basket makers rely on these tradesmen, commonly

indicators.note: common speech drops the h, so the first letter goes

parts.note: hosiers are sellers of stockings

explanation.surface: Basket weavers depend on these merchants, usually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' signals Cockney h-dropping.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow shoots are woven into baskets, so they are what basket weavers need.

clue.text: See 12
A natural hanger-on, Wally gets to blow the whistle

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a fool, as is a goose
to grass is to inform on someone

explanation.surface: A clingy fool becomes an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant, also called cleavers, has hooked bristles that stick to clothes and fur, hence a hanger-on from nature. WALLY is mild British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: This sticky weed clings to passers-by, so it is a hanger-on in the plant world.

clue.text: Put up deposit to secure tons of metal

indicators.note: to secure is to hold, so the sediment holds the letter
in a down clue put up means read the word from bottom to top

parts.note: lees are a wine deposit

explanation.surface: Pay a deposit to secure tons of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' looks like money; it is a sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron and carbon alloy is a strong metal.

clue.text: Bona fide 7 used 10

indicators.note: answer 10 is an adverb for at steady intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A genuine 7 used 10.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is the solution of 7-down and 10 is 10-across: take alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine or authentic things are real, a close synonym.

clue.text: A good place to learn game on cold morning

indicators.note: in an across clue, game placed on the others means it follows them

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A card game on a chilly morning makes a fine study opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient English university town is a renowned centre of learning.

clue.text: Garbage — three times as much left out

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is put out of the word for treble

parts.note: triple means three times as much

explanation.surface: Rubbish, three times over, but leaving some out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or worthless rubbish is called after cow's stomach lining, a cheap offal.

clue.text: Nijinsky, for instance, in back street in Paris

parts.note: dans is the French for in, signalled by the words in Paris

indicators.note: back says the French street word is read from its end

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: The great Russian dancer spotted down a Parisian back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back street' looks like one phrase, but 'back' turns RUE round. 'in Paris' makes both 'in' and 'street' French.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaslav Nijinsky was a celebrated male ballet dancer, the French term for which this is.

clue.text: Doctors at one time noted for their application?

definitions.meaning: physicians were once called by this old name
bloodsucking worms are known for being applied to the skin

explanation.surface: Old-time doctors were famous for their diligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' seems to mean hard work, but it is the placing of the worms on a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic physicians bore this name, and the bloodsucking worms they used were applied to patients.
